notes: Copilot long-idle: the row must survive an idle window longer than readyTTL purely because its PID is alive, then resume normally on the next prompt. Recorded with IRRLICHT_READY_SESSION_TTL=15s so the 15 s duration_at_least_ms cleanly exceeds the TTL (production is 30 min). The daemon-side mechanism is adapter-agnostic (pid_manager.go:1026 returns before the reap when the bound PID answers Kill(pid,0)), so the copilot-specific precondition is the PID bind — asserted explicitly as pid_bind rather than left implicit, because a 20 s window is too short for reapUnboundReadyGhost (>30 s stale UpdatedAt AND >2 min stale transcript) to turn a missing bind into a visible disappearance. State stability during the window is structural: every copilot event type that can fire while the user is away (session.usage_checkpoint, session.shutdown, model_change, auto_mode_resolved, system.message, assistant.turn_start, unknown future types) is Skip=true in the parser, so only user.message and assistant.turn_end can move state. PRESESSION SHAPE (provisional, from code): copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch with only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl on the first prompt, so processlifecycle.Scanner mints a proc-<PID> row before the fswatcher sees any transcript and the real session arrives under a DIFFERENT id — birth is two phases and every later phase, the idle window included, is anchored to the REAL session. OBSERVATIONS: tokens and cost are live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map (session.usage_checkpoint carries no token counts). model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only "auto" and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn — with two turns in this recipe the two could legitimately differ.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
Real <session-id> session reconciles under a different session id once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt, born ready
copilot PID bound to the real session by cwd — the live-PID short-circuit that must keep the row alive past readyTTL
First user prompt drives the real session ready → working
assistant.turn_end settles the first turn back to ready
Session does NOT disappear past readyTTL (15 s here) and state remains ready for the whole idle window
Next user prompt on the long-idle session: ready → working resumes normally, same session id
Second turn completes back to ready — final state ready, no tool calls, never waiting
